newsitem.title: USA: Virginia executes man for child murder and torture.
newsitem.headline: Virginia executes man for child murder and torture.

text.p: A Virginia man who abducted, tortured and murdered a 15-year-old boy was executed by lethal injection on Thursday night at the Greensville Correctional Centre.

Michael Carl George, 39, was convicted of the June 16, 1990, robbery and murder of Alexander Sztanko, whose genitals were burned with a stun gun. Lawyers for George did not file a clemency petition with the state's governor, George Allen.
His last meal was pizza, apple pie and diet 7-UP soda before he was put to death at 9:18 p.m. EST.
The execution is the first in Virginia this year. The state shares second place with Florida with 38 executions since the death penalty was reimposed in 1976.
Texas, with more than 100, leads the country in the number of executions. But last year Virginia executed eight people -- more than any other state.

Sztanko's parents reported him missing the night of June 16, 1990. The next day a police officer spotted George and found Sztanko's tennis shoes nearby. A bloodhound followed the boy's scent to George's Ford Bronco and then to the body.

The boy was shot once in the head, his penis was burned while he was still alive and semen was found on his body. No trace of his wallet and two $20 bills his parents thought he was carrying were found.

Searches of George's vehicle and home turned up handcuffs, the 9mm handgun used to kill Sztanko, a stun gun capable of causing the burns suffered by Sztanko and a map marked with the locations of Sztanko's body and his motorcycle.
The U.S. Supreme Court turned down the man's stay of execution 7-2 earlier on Thursday.
Gov. Allen said he did not receive a petition for clemency but reviewed records and court opinions on the case anyway.
"Michael Carl George hideously tortured and murdered 15-year-old Alexander Eugene Sztanko ...," the governor said.

"As a father, I am particularly aware of and sensitive to the profound pain and loss suffered by the parents of the victim taken from them at such a young age and in such a brutal manner. Our prayers are with them today."
